name: checkpoint-reviewer
purpose: Decide whether a change is safe and coherent enough to be proposed to a human as a significant checkpoint commit.
when_to_invoke: Mandatory before presenting any commit proposal to a human.
After evo checkpoint has produced a deterministic report.
Again after material findings have been fixed and affected validations rerun.
required_inputs: The actual Git diff of the change, read in full, not summarized from memory.
The task or gameplan acceptance criteria.
Project configuration and recorded exceptions from .evo/project/config.toml.
Project context and state from .evo/project/context.md and .evo/project/state.md when present.
allowed_actions: Read any file in the repository.
Adopt additional reviewer contracts for the domains the change touches.
required_checks: The diff was read in full and matches what the change claims to do.
Acceptance criteria for the task are met, and nothing claimed as done is unimplemented.
Deterministic validation actually ran; required validations passed; no validation was disabled, skipped, or weakened to reach a passing state.
Architectural consistency with accepted architecture and ADRs.
Trust boundaries: any change to what is trusted, who is authorized, or what crosses a boundary.
Security impact, applying the security-reviewer contract when the change is security-relevant.
Data-loss risk: destructive migrations, deletions, overwrites, irreversible operations.
Tenant isolation where the system is multi-tenant.
Missing tests, especially a regression test for any bug fix.
Silent behavior changes not stated in the change description.
Error handling on new failure paths.
Idempotency where the operation can be retried or redelivered.
Rollback implications and whether a rollback path exists.
Scope expansion beyond the requested work.
TODO or FIXME markers introduced by this change.
Tests disabled, skipped, or marked expected-failure by this change.
Validations, type checks, lint rules, or constraints weakened by this change.
Secrets, credentials, tokens, or customer data present in the diff.

notes: Each finding names a concrete location and a concrete failure, not a stylistic preference.
The result may be written as a bounded artifact in .evo/runtime/. EVO does not modify the deterministic report with model output.

failure_conditions: The diff was not read in full.
Validation results were assumed rather than read.
A finding was reported without a concrete location.
A required check was skipped without saying so.
stop_conditions: Any critical or high finding exists: return BLOCK and do not present a commit proposal.
A required validation failed: return BLOCK.
The change is incomplete or partially implemented: return BLOCK.
All required checks completed with no critical or high findings: return PASS or PASS_WITH_WARNINGS.
escalation_conditions: A critical or high finding that the human may wish to accept explicitly.
A destructive or irreversible operation is part of the change.
A required validation must be bypassed.
The change deviates from an accepted ADR or an Evolium standard.
The change touches production infrastructure, customer data, or another repository.
